references.text: This verse contains the blessing, which is the direct opposite of the curse in verse 18. The same expression is used: 'the fruit of your womb, the fruit of your ground, the calves of your herd and the lambs of your flock' - here as a blessing, in verse 18 as a curse.
Describes the Lord's blessing over the fruit of life, the fruit of the earth, and livestock - the same elements that the curse in verse 18 targets.

The promise of blessing over the fruit of life, the fruit of the earth, grain, wine, oil, and the offspring of livestock - the same terms used in the curse in 28:18. The terms 'shegar' (calves) and 'ashtarot' (lambs) appear in both places.
A promise of fertility and that no one shall be childless or barren - the opposite of the curse over the fruit of life in Deuteronomy 28:18.
Part of the curses in Leviticus describing that the land will not yield its produce - parallel to the curse over the fruit of the earth in 28:18.
Describes the devastation of the land and lack of harvest due to a locust plague - parallel to the curse over the fruit of the earth.
A promise of blessing over the fruit of the earth when the people bring tithes - contrasting with the curse over the fruit of the earth due to disobedience in 28:18.
